bullets.text: Platform architecture owner for a greenfield AI-native B2B marketplace; leads a 10-person engineering team and a product manager.
PLATFORM & GPU INFRASTRUCTURE
Architected and launched SwifTradeSupply.com end to end — system decomposition, data model, integration and security architecture, launch
sequencing — taking it from zero to production in five months; shipped July 2026.
Selected the GPU and AI compute substrate on benchmarked stability, cost per GPU-hour, model support and API-driven provisioning; that
Engineered cost per unit of work directly into the datapath: cheapest-first source layering that reaches paid APIs only after free sources are
exhausted, response caching with in-flight request coalescing, and per-run unit-cost accounting.
AI SYSTEMS IN PRODUCTION
Built GPU-accelerated catalog automation — multi-storefront listing generation via lexical and semantic matching with GPU image similarity,
plus master-category classification using embeddings and clustering — cutting supplier onboarding from days to minutes.
Architected a multi-agent buyer-acquisition pipeline on a LangGraph state machine — geo-targeted discovery, multi-source contact
enrichment, explainable lead scoring, personalized outreach — instrumented with LangSmith tracing for run-level observability and failure
Designed the output-governance layer for generated outbound: constrained assembly keeping every claim traceable to a verified source,
deterministic pre-send validation with a human review queue, a readiness gate that halts unsafe configuration, and automated reply
classification driving suppression.
Scaled Amazon-channel fulfillment 6.6× (300 → 2,000 orders/day) on the automation layer built in-house, delivering ~300K incremental orders
over the following six months against a platform lifetime total past 1M.
ENGINEERING LEADERSHIP
Led and developed a 10-person engineering team, establishing architecture review practice, AI-assisted development standards and QA
automation that measurably accelerated production delivery.
Built a company-wide model-benchmark framework scoring coding models and agentic harnesses on cost, code correctness, iterations to
convergence and latency, then standardized the toolchain and an automated code-review loop on the results.
Architecture lead for consumer video and edge platforms; 3M+ Fios Video and 1M+ OTT devices in the field.
GPU INFRASTRUCTURE & AI PIPELINES
Architected a Whisper ASR and LLM analysis pipeline on NVIDIA Tesla GPUs for early field-issue detection, processing 2,000+ hours of noisy
narrowband telephony at 75% transcription accuracy with CUDA workloads tuned for throughput and cost per hour of audio; authored the
business case quantifying a ~25% call-deflection opportunity.
Ran the comparative datapath analysis for high-rate packet ingestion into GPU-accelerated pipelines — DPDK kernel-bypass versus
SmartNIC/DPU offload — scored against latency budgets, throughput ceilings and per-node hardware cost; the result set the platform's offload
direction.
Diagnosed DGX A100 (8×A100, 640 GB) multi-GPU server and ProLiant DL385 subsystem failures via BMC/iLO and IPMI, hardening the GPU
compute tier.
PLATFORM ARCHITECTURE & TECHNICAL LEADERSHIP
Led 25+ cross-functional HW/FW/SW engineering teams delivering quarterly releases across Stream TV, set-top boxes, soundbars, remote
devices and CE applications; developed engineers through architecture review.
Authored the production-grade architecture and design specifications for thin-client hardware, MEC deployment, security and A/V pipelines —
the reference documents ODM and internal teams built against.
Architected an edge-native virtual mobile computing platform (independent R&D): thin-client hardware, Android containerization at the MEC
tier, latency-sensitive A/V transport and zero-trust security; advanced through prototyping, published as a whitepaper, provisional patent
application filed.
Owned regulatory and industry certification programs end to end — FCC Part 15 (B/C/E), UL 62368-1, Wi-Fi Alliance, Bluetooth SIG, Energy
Star — from design review through lab submission and grant.
PLATFORM RELIABILITY & NON-FUNCTIONAL REQUIREMENTS
Root-caused systemic field failures across a 4M+ device fleet — MoCA link instability, 802.11 interference, A/V dropouts, DVR faults, update
freezes — driving causes back into platform architecture rather than point fixes.
Designed the DVR high-throughput storage datapath sustaining 24 parallel I/O streams under heavy disk contention, with fragmentation
mitigation and write-coalescence algorithms for real-time record and playback.
Designed eMMC flash layouts, boot state machines and update frameworks, cutting field update time by ~15 seconds.
Built bootloaders, device drivers, IR firmware and platform diagnostics that measurably improved field reliability.
Engineered Linux kernel modules and high-performance middleware tuned for memory, IPC, networking and real-time constraints.
Executed ARM/x86 board bring-up, MoCA 2.0 PHY/MAC driver debugging and eMMC flash architecture.
classification and forwarding offload; built an enterprise Windows security platform for 500–1,000 network endpoints.

RTOS; improved 802.11 PHY/MAC performance.
